type.instructions: Which Conventional Commits type fits this change?

criteria.build: The change alters how the package is built, packaged or locked, such as build settings, the lock file or a dependency version.
criteria.chore: The change is repository upkeep that alters no shipped code, test, documentation, build or CI behaviour, such as tool or agent settings, hook settings or release bookkeeping.
criteria.ci: The change alters the continuous integration workflows, jobs or scripts that run on the CI service.
criteria.docs: The change alters only documentation, such as README text, docs pages, docstrings, comments or status notes.
criteria.feat: The change adds a new capability that users of the library, CLI or server can call or observe.
criteria.fix: The change corrects behaviour that was wrong, broken or did not match its documented contract.
criteria.perf: The change makes existing behaviour faster or use fewer resources without changing what it does.
criteria.refactor: The change restructures code without changing its behaviour, and it neither adds a capability nor fixes a defect.
criteria.test: The change adds or corrects tests, test fixtures or test helpers, and it changes no production code.

closes.instructions: Does this commit finish the issue it names?

criteria.closes: The commit completes every remaining Done-when item of the issue it names, so the issue can close when the commit lands.
criteria.refs: The commit does only part of the issue it names, such as partial, preparatory or follow-up work, so the issue stays open.
